saints.name: Ioannikios the Great

summary.text: A former soldier who became a Byzantine monk and hermit. The OCA associates him with a short prayer addressed to the Holy Trinity.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The OCA life gives Marikat in Bithynia as his birthplace and 752 as his birth year. It describes a poor childhood spent tending the family’s cattle.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: After six years in imperial military service, he sought monastic solitude. An elder first required community life; he learned to read and write and memorized Psalms. His later life included solitary prayer, monastic tonsure, and residence at several ascetic sites.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The life records his repose on November 4, 846, aged ninety-four. It describes a monastic death, rather than execution.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: His remembrance combines psalmody with a Trinitarian prayer still used in Orthodox prayer books. The OCA also recounts healings and deliverances as part of his received hagiographic life.
